items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your average blood sugar was 306.2 mg/dL, which is above 250, so contact your care team today. Only 0.0% of your readings were in the 70-180 range, which is why you should reach out to them now.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal went with a smaller rise in blood sugar, about 3.2 mg/dL smaller in real adults. Walking 10 to 19 minutes after dinner got most of the gain, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: About 26.7% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later, and sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. Try to start dinner before 8 pm, as sugar also rose about 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than after one before 6 pm.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 14.4 hours, with 92.3% of nights reaching 13 hours. In the program, adding the overnight fast to coaching changed the results by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone.
